context: A screenshot of ghent-live, a 3D map of the historic centre of Ghent (Belgium) around the Belfry, rendered in a web browser from sample data. A red ring with a thin red beam marks the Belfry. The ground is still a plain placeholder grid: streets, buildings and water come from other layers that are not drawn here. The layer under test is the shared-bike stations.

checks.name: bike_bars
checks.instructions: Thin vertical bars stand on the ground in two or more clearly different colours.

checks.name: bars_along_streets
checks.instructions: Thin vertical bars in two or more colours stand along the streets. The streets themselves are not drawn here, so judge by the bars: they stand in rows and lines that bend and branch like streets, not in a regular grid or in one blob.

checks.name: bar_heights
checks.instructions: The bars have different heights: most are short stubs, and some stand clearly taller.

checks.name: bars_thin
checks.instructions: Every bar is a thin post, several times taller than it is wide; none is a wide block or a thick column.
